days.title: What Must No Muslim Be Ignorant Of?
days.question: Are there things in the religion that every Muslim must know, with no excuse for not knowing them?
days.principle: There is basic, essential knowledge that no Muslim may be ignorant of. It distinguishes him from the people of misguidance, especially in matters of belief and the major questions of the lawful and the unlawful. It is the firmly established law that every Muslim must know and hold to.

misconception.peopleSay: Knowing about the religion is the job of scholars and specialists only; an ordinary person is not required to know anything.
misconception.correct: There is a portion that is obligatory on everyone: what no person may be ignorant of among the obligations placed on him, such as the two testimonies of faith, belief in the Resurrection, the obligation of the five daily prayers and the fast of Ramadan. There are also things whose general ruling he must know and for which ignorance is no excuse, such as the prohibition of zina, riba and alcohol.

days.action: On a sheet of paper, write the list Ibn Abd al-Barr gave of the things no Muslim may be ignorant of, and mark the one you feel you most need to learn in the coming days.
lesson: This book starts from an important observation: many intellectual distortions have crept into Muslims' minds, to the point that some people no longer see any contradiction between Islam and ideas that oppose it. So the authors saw an urgent need to gather the basic knowledge no Muslim may be ignorant of. This is the knowledge by which a person's Islam is valid in this world and by which he attains salvation in the Hereafter. Ibn Abd al-Barr summarised it: that we testify to Allah's oneness and to Muhammad ﷺ being His Messenger; that we believe in the Resurrection, Paradise and Hellfire, and that the Quran is the speech of Allah; that we know the rulings of prayer and fasting, of zakah if we have wealth, and of Hajj if we have wealth and ability. We must also know the clear prohibitions, such as zina, riba, alcohol, oppression and consuming people's wealth unjustly. The project is planned in two stages: the first for every Muslim, and the second for particular groups such as merchants, doctors and callers to Islam. The authors reassure us that they included only authentic (sahih) or good (hasan) hadiths in the book.
days.quote: In this study we have included only the authentic (sahih) or good (hasan) hadiths of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even though some scholars allow citing weak hadiths in matters of fiqh; we found in the authentic hadiths sufficiency, indeed abundance.

quiz.question: Someone says: "I'm not a sheikh, so I don't need to know anything about the religion." Is that right?
options: Right, all religious knowledge is an obligation on scholars only
Wrong, there is a portion of knowledge every Muslim must have, such as the obligations upon him
Right, as long as his intention is good he doesn't need to learn
Right, it is enough for him to ask when he needs to, and nothing is required of him
quiz.explanation: Ibn Abd al-Barr says, while discussing the knowledge that is obligatory on all Muslims and that none of them may be ignorant of…

quiz.question: A young man has just been given a lot of money by Allah. What does he now have to learn about the religion because of this money?
options: The rulings of zakah: on what it is due, when, and how much
Nothing extra; zakah is only for big merchants
He learns it after being rich for ten years
It is enough to give whatever charity he likes without knowing anything
quiz.explanation: And if he has wealth, he is obliged to know on what zakah is due, when it is due, and how much is due.

quiz.question: A Muslim doctor or merchant: are there things in the religion they must know beyond what an ordinary Muslim knows?
options: No, religion has nothing to do with professions
No, exactly the same amount is required of everyone
Yes, but it is optional and not binding at all
Yes, everyone with a profession needs to know the rulings that concern their work
quiz.explanation: The second stage: in it the address is directed to particular groups, such as professionals among merchants, doctors and the like.

askTheBook: What does "what no Muslim may be ignorant of" mean?
What did Ibn Abd al-Barr say about the obligations every Muslim must know?
How many stages is this book's project made of, and who is each stage for?

days.title: You Are Part of a Great Ummah
days.question: If you moved to another country or took another nationality, would that change your belonging to the Muslim Ummah?
days.principle: Every Muslim believes that he is part of the Muslim Ummah, the nation of the final message, which is united on the foundation of being pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet and Messenger, and on disavowing every religion that contradicts Islam.

misconception.peopleSay: The Ummah is weak now, so belonging to it and taking pride in it is pointless.
misconception.correct: The stumble the Ummah is going through is a passing one, caused by its weak adherence to the Quran and Sunnah. It does not stop a Muslim from belonging to the Ummah and taking pride in it. This Ummah held the position of leadership for more than ten centuries, and the truths of revelation make it certain that Islam will rise again.

days.action: Choose one of the qualities of the Ummah mentioned in the book (such as the Ummah of loyalty and mercy, or the Ummah of moderation and balance) and explain what it means to a family member or friend today.
lesson: The first thing the introduction says is that none of us is an isolated individual; each of us is a member of an Ummah whose history spans fourteen centuries, led by the Prophet ﷺ and those who followed his way among the imams of knowledge and religion. This certainty does not waver however much a Muslim travels or lives abroad, whatever nationalities he acquires or parties and institutions he joins. The book describes this Ummah with beautiful qualities: it is the Ummah of response, which believed in the Prophet ﷺ and supported him, and an Ummah that refers its judgements to the revelation Allah Himself has undertaken to preserve. It is also a merciful Ummah, like one body, however different its lands, races and colours, and a balanced Ummah, free of both excess and neglect. If the Ummah is going through weakness now, the book explains that it is a passing stumble caused by weak adherence to the Quran and Sunnah. It also says that attempts to divide the Muslim world are remnants of colonialism, and a Muslim must not make them the basis of his loyalty and disavowal.
days.quote: However much a Muslim travels the earth… however far east or west he goes, however much he is pursued or pressured in the lands of Islam… however much he is given power or showered with favours in the lands of disbelief… whatever nationalities he acquires… or parties and institutions he joins… his unshakeable certainty is that he is part of this blessed Ummah.

quiz.question: A Muslim living abroad took the nationality of another country. What does that change about his belonging to the Muslim Ummah?
options: It takes him out of the Ummah because he now belongs to another country
It makes him only half a member of the Ummah
It changes nothing; his certainty that he is part of the Ummah stays firm whatever his nationality
His belonging is determined by the nationality in his passport
quiz.explanation: Whatever nationalities he acquires… or parties and institutions he joins… his unshakeable certainty is that he is part of this blessed Ummah.

quiz.question: Someone says: "The Ummah is weak now, so there's no point being proud to belong to it." What is the correct understanding?
options: The weakness proves the Ummah is finished
This weakness is a passing stumble caused by weak adherence to the Quran and Sunnah, and it does not cancel belonging and pride
Taking pride in the Ummah is not required at all
This weakness is a permanent fate with no way out
quiz.explanation: He realises that it is a passing stumble, caused by its weak adherence to the Quran and Sunnah.

quiz.question: What is the foundation that unites Muslims into one Ummah?
options: Being pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion and Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet and Messenger
A single language
A single country and borders
A single colour and race
quiz.explanation: His unshakeable certainty is that he is part of this blessed Ummah.

askTheBook: What does "the Ummah of response" mean?
What qualities of the Muslim Ummah does the introduction mention?
What does the book say about attempts to divide the Muslim world?

days.title: Tawhid: The Story That Began with the First Human
days.question: Did people worship Allah alone from the very beginning, or did tawhid come later?
days.principle: We believe that pure tawhid is the natural disposition (fitrah) upon which Allah created His servants, and that it is the foundation of all the heavenly messages; whatever worship of other than Allah appeared afterwards is shirk and an innovated distortion.

misconception.peopleSay: In the past people worshipped many gods, and tawhid is an idea that came late.
misconception.correct: Pure tawhid is the fitrah upon which Allah created His servants and the foundation of all the messages. Any worship of other than Allah, or attributing a son to Allah, that happened afterwards is shirk and an innovated distortion that all the prophets disavow.

days.action: Memorise today the six pillars of faith in the order given in the hadith, and say them to yourself before you sleep.
lesson: The first chapter of the book begins with the six pillars of faith: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree, its good and its bad. It then explains that tawhid is not a new idea; it is the fitrah Allah created people upon from the start. Allah took a covenant from the descendants of Adam that He is their Lord, and they bore witness to it, so that no one could say on the Day of Resurrection that he was unaware or was only following his forefathers. The Prophet ﷺ said that every child is born upon the fitrah, and then his parents change him. All the prophets had one call: worship Allah alone and avoid false gods. That is why the Prophet ﷺ described them as brothers from different mothers (ikhwah li-'allat): united in tawhid and differing in the details of their laws.
days.quote: Allah informs us that He brought forth the descendants of Adam from their loins, bearing witness against themselves that Allah is their Lord and Sovereign and that there is no god but Him, just as He created them upon that and made it part of their nature.

quiz.question: Your friend says: "Humans at first worshipped many gods, and tawhid developed later." What is the correct understanding?
options: He is right, tawhid is a late idea
Tawhid and shirk existed equally from the beginning
No one can know what was there at the beginning
Tawhid is the origin and the fitrah, and shirk is what appeared afterwards
quiz.explanation: Allah informs us that He brought forth the descendants of Adam from their loins, bearing witness against themselves that Allah is their Lord and Sovereign and that there is no god but Him, just as He created them upon that and made it part of their nature.

quiz.question: Was the call of all the prophets one and the same, or different?
options: Different in tawhid and in their laws
Identical in every detail, even the laws
One in tawhid, and different in the details of the laws
Each prophet called to a different god
quiz.explanation: Meaning: they agreed in tawhid and differed in the details of their laws.

quiz.question: A child was born in a non-Muslim home. According to the hadith, what was he born upon?
options: His parents' religion from the first moment
The fitrah, and his parents are the ones who change him afterwards
No religion at all
Only whatever he will choose when he grows up

askTheBook: What are the six pillars of faith?
What does it mean that tawhid is the fitrah?
What does it mean that the prophets are brothers from different mothers?

days.title: Without Faith, Deeds Are Not Accepted
days.question: If someone does many good things but is not a believer, will Allah accept them from him?
days.principle: No prophet of Allah would ever call people to worship himself instead of Allah. Faith is a condition for acts of worship to be valid and accepted, and shirk and disbelief nullify all acts of obedience.

misconception.peopleSay: What matters is doing good; it doesn't matter whether you are a believer or not, Allah will accept it.
misconception.correct: Faith is a condition for acts of worship to be valid and accepted, and shirk and disbelief nullify all acts of obedience. Allah made faith together with righteous deeds the condition for a good life, entering Paradise and safety on the Day of Resurrection.

days.action: Read verse 97 of Surat an-Nahl and think: what are the two conditions Allah linked to a good life? Write them in one sentence in your own words.
lesson: The book continues: all the prophets called to the worship of Allah alone, and no prophet could ever tell people to worship him instead of Allah. If that is not allowed for prophets, it is even less allowed for anyone else. The Quran also denies that the Messiah, peace be upon him, told people to take him and his mother as two gods, and denies that Allah has taken a son. Then the book establishes an important rule: faith is a condition for worship to be accepted, just as prayer is not accepted without wudu. In many verses Allah linked a good life, entering Paradise and safety on the Day of Resurrection to righteous deeds together with faith. That is why, when the Prophet ﷺ sent Mu'adh to Yemen, he told him to start with tawhid before prayer.
days.quote: Just as no prayer is accepted without wudu, no worship is accepted without faith.

quiz.question: Someone does a lot of good and helps people, but does not believe in Allah. Are these deeds accepted by Allah?
options: No, faith is a condition for deeds to be accepted
Yes, good deeds are accepted from anyone
Only half of them are accepted
They are accepted if there are enough of them
quiz.explanation: Just as no prayer is accepted without wudu, no worship is accepted without faith.

quiz.question: If you were introducing someone to Islam, what would you start with?
options: The five daily prayers
The detailed rulings of transactions
Zakah
Tawhid: affirming that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah

quiz.question: If someone said a prophet could ask people to worship him, does that agree with the creed?
options: Yes, if he is a great prophet
Yes, it was allowed in the past
No, no prophet may call people to worship him instead of Allah
Possibly, if Allah permitted him
quiz.explanation: Allah informs us that it is not fitting for any prophet of Allah to call people to worship himself instead of Allah.

askTheBook: Why is faith a condition for acts of worship to be accepted?
Which verses say that shirk nullifies deeds?
What did the Prophet ﷺ tell Mu'adh to start with when calling the people of Yemen?

days.title: Allah Exists, and Your Heart Knows It
days.question: How do I know that Allah exists? Is there evidence inside me myself?
days.principle: We believe in the existence of Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and that He alone is the Creator of everything, the Owner of everything and the Disposer of everything; the first of the proofs of this is the proof of the fitrah.

misconception.peopleSay: An atheist never feels the existence of God at all.
misconception.correct: Acknowledging Allah's Lordship is innate; the righteous and the wicked both feel it. Ease and well-being, or distraction and heedlessness, may veil it, but it quickly collapses under the blows of hardship, and the disbelieving atheist turns to his Lord in humble supplication.

days.action: Remember a hard situation you went through in which you found yourself calling on Allah from your heart, and think about how that is an example of the proof of the fitrah the book speaks about.
lesson: The oneness of Lordship (tawhid ar-rububiyyah) means believing that Allah exists, and that He alone created everything, owns it and disposes of it. The book says the proofs of Allah's existence are as many as His creatures, from the smallest atom to the largest galaxy. The first proof is the fitrah: a feeling inside every person, good or bad, that he has a Creator. This feeling can be covered over in times of comfort and heedlessness, but as soon as hardship comes, a person finds himself calling on Allah. The Quran tells of people at sea who, when the waves covered them, called on Allah, sincere to Him in religion. Even Pharaoh's people denied the signs with their tongues while they were certain of them in themselves.
days.quote: The proofs of Allah's existence are as many as Allah's creatures! Everything Allah has created in the heavens and the earth carries within itself the most eloquent proof of the existence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

quiz.question: Someone says he is an atheist, and when he was in real danger he found himself calling on God. What does that show?
options: That he was only afraid, and it shows nothing
That acknowledging the Creator is an innate disposition in people that appears in times of hardship
That he learned it from the people around him
That this disposition exists only in believers
quiz.explanation: The first of the proofs of this is the proof of the fitrah.

quiz.question: What is meant by the oneness of Lordship (tawhid ar-rububiyyah)?
options: That Allah alone is the Creator, Owner and Disposer of everything
That Allah alone deserves worship
That He has names and attributes
That the universe created itself through a system
quiz.explanation: The proofs of Allah's existence are as many as Allah's creatures! Everything Allah has created in the heavens and the earth carries within itself the most eloquent proof of the existence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Humans may have come about without anyone creating them." What is the rational answer in the verse?
options: Humans created themselves gradually
There is no rational answer; faith is in the heart only
They may have been created by chance
Humans neither came into existence without a cause nor created themselves, so they must have a Creator, and He is Allah
quiz.explanation: Meaning: neither this nor that; rather Allah is the One who created them and brought them into being after they had been nothing worth mentioning.

askTheBook: What does the oneness of Lordship mean?
What is the proof of the fitrah for Allah's existence?
Why do people turn back to Allah in times of hardship?

days.title: Everything Around You Says: There Is a Creator
days.question: If I look around at the universe and the things I use, how does that point me to Allah?
days.principle: Created things, in all their number, are proofs that their Creator exists; all nations agree in affirming the Creator; and reason bears witness that every act has a doer, and that an act mirrors the power and some of the attributes of its doer.

misconception.peopleSay: Things can come out of nothing by themselves without anyone making them.
misconception.correct: Nothingness creates nothing. This is a rational necessity and a truth of the Shariah, attested by the self-evident sense of the mind and affirmed by the Book of the Lord of the worlds.

days.action: Choose one thing you use every day (like your phone or a light bulb) and explain to someone how its existence points to a maker with power and expertise, like the lamp example in the book.
lesson: The second proof of Allah's existence is created things themselves, because these magnificent things were neither created from nothing nor created themselves. The third proof is that all nations have affirmed the Creator's existence, and no known group of humans denied it except a few outliers whose words do not count. Then the book tells us about the evidence of reason, which rests on three foundations. The first is that every act has a doer: you cannot even imagine that your shoes, clothes or car were made without a maker. The second is that an act mirrors the power of its doer, just as a lamp tells you its maker has expertise in electricity. That is why the Quran urges us to reflect on the rain and the reviving of the earth after its death, because they make us know Allah's power and mercy.
days.quote: Coming to know some of the attributes of a doer by observing his acts and their effects is a rational and religious method; the mind perceives it by necessity, and the texts of the Shariah urge it.

quiz.question: You see a well-made phone. What does your mind tell you about whoever made it?
options: It may have assembled itself
It doesn't necessarily have a maker
That it has a maker, and the craftsmanship points to his power and expertise
The craftsmanship says nothing about the maker
quiz.explanation: When we see an electric lamp, we know that the maker of that lamp has glass and wires…

quiz.question: What has humanity's general position been on the existence of the Creator?
options: Most nations denied His existence
All nations affirmed the Creator's existence, and no known group denied it
Belief in the Creator appeared only with modern religions
Nations were split evenly in half
quiz.explanation: All the nations affirm Him and agree on that, such that no known group of the children of Adam held the opposite.

quiz.question: How can we come to know some of Allah's attributes without seeing Him?
options: By reflecting on His acts and their effects in the universe
We cannot know anything about His attributes
By imagining and picturing
Only from what people say
quiz.explanation: Coming to know some of the attributes of a doer by observing his acts and their effects is a rational and religious method; the mind perceives it by necessity, and the texts of the Shariah urge it.

askTheBook: How do created things point to Allah's existence?
What does the agreement of nations on the Creator's existence mean?
What are the foundations of the rational evidence for Allah's existence?

days.title: Who Is Able to Create?
days.question: Could nature, or anything in the universe, be what created the universe?
days.principle: An act is not attributed to one who is incapable of it, and there is nothing among created things to which creation can rightly be attributed; so the Creator of the universe must be other than the created universe.

misconception.peopleSay: Nature is what created the universe.
misconception.correct: There is nothing among created things to which creation can rightly be attributed; and since nothing among created things can rightly be credited with creation, the Creator of the universe must be other than the created universe or created nature.

days.action: When you hear someone attribute something to nature, remember the third foundation and think: can this nature be described as wise, all-knowing and living?
lesson: The universe, with its order and harmony, testifies that it is the work of One who exists eternally: great, all-powerful, living, wise and all-knowing, and a single, all-controlling Ruler. This is what the book calls the first and second foundations when we apply them to the universe. The third foundation says that an act is not attributed to one who is incapable of it. You cannot say that a mute person is the most eloquent speaker, or that an animal launched a spacecraft. By the same logic, we cannot attribute creation, provision, benefit and harm to deaf stones or to any created thing. So the book concludes that the Creator of the universe must be other than the universe itself and other than created nature.
days.quote: It is unthinkable to attribute eloquence of tongue and fine expression to a mute person.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Nature is what created living things." What rational rule answers him?
options: Nature really does have the power to create
There is no rational rule on this matter
Nature and Allah are partners in creation
An act cannot be attributed to one incapable of it, and nature itself is created
quiz.explanation: The third foundation: an act is not attributed to one who is incapable of it.

quiz.question: Why can't we attribute creation to any created being, however great?
options: Because great creatures can create small things
Only because they do not speak
Because no created being has the wisdom, knowledge and everlasting life that creating requires
We can if the creature is an angel
quiz.explanation: Because there is nothing among them that can be described as the Wise, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, the Magnificent, the All-Controlling, the Guide, the Ever-Living, the Everlasting, the Abiding.

quiz.question: Someone believes a stone or statue brings him benefit or protects him from harm. What does reason say?
options: Possibly, if it is blessed
Impossible; a stone is incapable of creating, providing, benefiting or harming
Possibly, if people agree on it
That depends on each person's belief
quiz.explanation: Just as it is unthinkable to attribute to deaf stones the power to create, provide, give life and cause death, and to bring benefit and harm to whomever they wish.

askTheBook: What does "an act is not attributed to one incapable of it" mean?
What attributes does the universe testify to in its Creator?
Why can't we say that nature created the universe?

days.title: All Worship Belongs to Allah
days.question: Is worship only prayer and fasting, or is it something broader?
days.principle: We believe in singling out Allah alone for worship and disavowing everything worshipped besides Him, and that directing worship to other than Allah breaks tawhid and is disbelief in faith.

misconception.peopleSay: Worship is only prayer and fasting; the rest of my life has nothing to do with worship.
misconception.correct: Worship is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with, of outward and inward words and deeds.

days.action: Today, while praying, reflect in your heart on the verse ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ (al-An'am 162), and think of one ordinary act in your day that you can do with the intention of pleasing Allah.
lesson: The oneness of worship (tawhid al-uluhiyyah) means singling out Allah alone for worship and disavowing anything worshipped besides Him. Worship is not only prayer and fasting; it is everything Allah loves and is pleased with, of words and deeds, outward or in the heart. Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to say that his prayer, his sacrifice, his life and his death are all for Allah, Lord of the worlds, with no partner. The book explains that the gods the polytheists worship are helpless creatures that neither benefit nor harm, neither hear nor see, and their worshippers are more complete than they are. Strangely, some people used to worship a group of jinn; those jinn became Muslim, yet the people kept clinging to their worship. That is why Allah forbade us to call on, besides Him, what neither benefits nor harms us.
days.quote: These gods they claim besides Allah cannot remove harm from those who worship them, so how could they deserve to be worshipped besides Allah?!

quiz.question: Is worship only prayer and fasting?
options: No, worship is every outward or inward word or deed that Allah loves and is pleased with
Yes, only the rituals are worship
Worship is only acts of the heart
Worship is only what is done in the mosque
quiz.explanation: Worship is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with, of outward and inward words and deeds.

quiz.question: Someone slaughters an animal for other than Allah as an act of devotion. What is the ruling?
options: Just a custom with no ruling
Only disliked
Permissible if his intention is ultimately to get closer to Allah
Directing worship to other than Allah, which breaks tawhid
quiz.explanation: Meaning: make your prayer and your sacrifice sincerely for Him.

quiz.question: Why can't we worship other than Allah, even someone righteous or a great creature?
options: We can if it brings us closer to Allah
We can if it is a prophet
Because everything worshipped besides Allah has no power to remove harm from its worshipper
No problem as long as the heart is with Allah
quiz.explanation: These gods they claim besides Allah cannot remove harm from those who worship them, so how could they deserve to be worshipped besides Allah?!

askTheBook: What does the oneness of worship mean?
How does the book define worship?
Why is worshipping other than Allah meaningless?

days.title: Love, Seeking Refuge and Praise All Have Limits
days.question: Can a person fall into shirk while thinking he is just loving or praising the righteous?
days.principle: Whoever loves something besides Allah as he loves Allah has taken rivals besides Allah. Seeking refuge is an act of worship, so whoever directs any of it to other than Allah has made that a partner with Allah. Excess regarding the righteous was the root of shirk among the children of Adam.

misconception.peopleSay: Exaggerating in praising the righteous and the Prophet ﷺ is love, and there is no problem with it however far it goes.
misconception.correct: Excess regarding the righteous was the root of shirk among the children of Adam. The Prophet ﷺ forbade excess, saying: Do not over-praise me as the Christians over-praised the son of Mary; I am only a servant. Over-praising (itra') is exceeding the limit in praise and lying in it.

days.action: Today, watch how you talk about people you love: do not describe anyone with something that is not theirs, just as the Prophet ﷺ stopped the girl who attributed knowledge of the unseen to him.
lesson: Shirk is not only bowing to an idol; it can be in love, when a person loves something as he loves Allah. It can be in seeking refuge, as the Arabs of the Jahiliyyah used to seek refuge with the jinn when they camped in a desolate valley, and the jinn only increased them in fear and terror. The Prophet ﷺ cursed whoever slaughters for other than Allah. The book relates that the idols of Nuh's people, such as Wadd and Suwa', were originally the names of righteous men; after they died, Shaytan made it attractive to people to make statues of them, and when knowledge was forgotten they were worshipped. That is why the Prophet ﷺ said: do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians did with the son of Mary; I am Allah's servant and messenger. And when a girl said that the Prophet knows what will happen tomorrow, he stopped her and told her to go back to what she had been saying.
days.quote: Over-praising (itra') is exceeding the limit in praise and lying in it.

quiz.question: Someone loves a person or thing so much that he puts its pleasure before Allah's and loves it as he loves Allah. What is the ruling?
options: Normal, love is a feeling with no ruling
He has taken it as a rival to Allah; this love is worship that may not be directed to other than Allah
Only disliked
Permissible as long as he prays
quiz.explanation: Excess regarding the righteous was the root of shirk among the children of Adam.

quiz.question: Someone praises the Prophet ﷺ with words that contain attributes of Allah. What is the ruling?
options: This is forbidden over-praising, because it exceeds the limit in praise
The more praise the better
Permissible as long as it comes from love
Recommended on special occasions
quiz.explanation: Over-praising (itra') is exceeding the limit in praise and lying in it.

quiz.question: A girl was singing and said about the Prophet ﷺ that he knows what will happen tomorrow. What did the Prophet ﷺ do?
options: He agreed because it was praise
He kept silent about that line
He stopped her from singing altogether
He stopped her from saying that line and let her carry on with the rest

askTheBook: What is the shirk of love?
How did the idols come to be worshipped among Nuh's people?
Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid over-praising him?

days.title: Who Makes Things Lawful and Unlawful?
days.question: Who has the right to say "this is halal" and "this is haram": people, or Allah?
days.principle: The One who alone created this universe alone has the right to guide His servants. Nothing is lawful except what Allah and His Messenger made lawful, and nothing is unlawful except what Allah and His Messenger made unlawful; the decisive proof and the highest judgement is the Quran and Sunnah and nothing else.

misconception.peopleSay: Religion belongs in the mosque; rulings and laws are for people to set however they like.
misconception.correct: The decisive proof and the highest judgement is the Quran and Sunnah. Moving the source of rulings from revelation to whims, as the advocates of secularism promote, is associating partners with Allah and disbelief in His oneness.

days.action: When you come to decide whether something is halal or haram, first ask yourself: what did Allah and His Messenger say? Try this in one situation today.
lesson: The book links two things: the One who alone created the universe is the One who alone has the right to guide and command His servants. So nothing is halal except what Allah and His Messenger made halal, and nothing is haram except what Allah and His Messenger made haram. When Muslims differ, the reference is the Quran and Sunnah, and Allah made referring disputes to them a sign of faith in Allah and the Last Day. When Allah and His Messenger have ruled on something, no one has any choice or opinion that contradicts it. The book explains that after the Prophet ﷺ, infallibility belongs only to the Ummah as a whole, because Allah has protected it from agreeing on misguidance. It also warns that moving rulings from revelation to whims, as the advocates of secularism call for, is associating partners with Allah.
days.quote: So He made referring matters to Allah and His Messenger the basis of faith in Allah and the Last Day.

quiz.question: Someone says: "What is halal and haram should be decided by the majority opinion of people." What is the correct understanding?
options: The majority really does decide
Each person decides for himself
Halal is what Allah and His Messenger made halal, and haram is what Allah and His Messenger made haram
Customs are the main reference
quiz.explanation: When Allah and His Messenger have ruled on something, no one may oppose it, and no one has any choice, opinion or say in it.

quiz.question: When Muslims differ on a question, what should they refer it to?
options: The opinion of the strongest among them
They refer it to Allah and His Messenger, and this is a sign of faith
Customs and traditions
Everyone keeps his own opinion
quiz.explanation: So He made referring matters to Allah and His Messenger the basis of faith in Allah and the Last Day.

quiz.question: Is there any scholar or sheikh after the Prophet ﷺ whose words are infallible and never to be reconsidered?
options: No, after the Prophet ﷺ infallibility belongs only to the Ummah as a whole
Yes, the senior scholars are infallible
Yes, the sheikh of each country
Anyone who speaks about religion is infallible
quiz.explanation: And that infallibility is not established for anyone after the Prophet ﷺ except the Ummah as a whole.

askTheBook: What does a single source of guidance mean?
Who has the right to make things lawful and unlawful?
What does the book say about moving rulings from revelation to whims?
